subtitle: A commander carves his service into stone beneath the Kakatiya sky

panels.shot: majestic low-angle wide of a lone stone pillar rising before the Rudreshvara temple at Palampet
panels.action: Recherla Rudra stands beside the towering carved pillar at Palampet, hand resting on its weathered stone, the Rudreshvara temple and shimmering tank behind him under a vast Telangana sky.

dialogue.text: In the Kakatiya age, Recherla Rudra was no king, yet his 201-line pillar at Palampet still speaks of battles, villages and a temple that turned loyal service into stone memory.

i18n.hi: काकतीय युग में रुद्र राजा नहीं था, फिर भी पलमपेट का उसका २०१-पंक्ति स्तंभ आज भी युद्धों, गाँवों और उस मंदिर की बात करता है जिसने वफादार सेवा को पत्थर की याद बना दिया

panels.shot: slow push-in on the carved surface of the pillar, letters catching the light
panels.action: Close view of the Palampet pillar’s packed Telugu-Kannada script, each shallow letter lit by the slanting sun, the Rudreshvara shrine blurred in the distance.

dialogue.text: The pillar is dated 31 March 1213 CE. Two hundred and one lines name generals, villages and grants. Behind every word stands a living network in the Kakatiya realm.

i18n.hi: यह स्तंभ ३१ मार्च १२१३ ई. का है। दो सौ एक पंक्तियाँ सेनापतियों, गाँवों और दान का ब्योरा देती हैं। हर शब्द के पीछे काकतीय राज्य की जीवित जाल बिछी है

panels.shot: wide historical tableau of Warangal fort and court, with Rudra small among many officers
panels.action: Warangal’s stone fort walls and great gateway rise behind a bustling courtyard where Recherla Rudra, in modest commander’s attire, stands among other captains and ministers before a seated Kakatiya ruler.

dialogue.text: Around 1200, the Kakatiya court at Warangal thrummed with captains and ministers. Recherla Rudra served among them, part of a web of commanders that held the kingdom together.

i18n.hi: १२०० के आसपास वरंगल की काकतीय सभा सेनानायकों और मंत्रियों से गूंजती थी। रेचेर्ला रुद्र भी उनमें था, उन कमांडरों के जाल का हिस्सा जो राज्य को थामे हुए थे

panels.shot: medium shot of Rudra receiving a written order from a royal emissary
panels.action: In a shaded Warangal hall, Recherla Rudra bows slightly as a royal emissary hands him a palm-leaf order, other officers watching with measured respect.

dialogue.text: The inscriptions call Rudra a commander, not a king. His authority flowed from royal orders, earned through service, and anchored in lands and men entrusted to him.

i18n.hi: लेखों में रुद्र को सेनानायक कहा गया है, राजा नहीं। उसका अधिकार राजाज्ञा से आता है, सेवा से कमाया है, और उसके हवाले की गई ज़मीन व लोगों पर टिकता है

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of Rudra with elders, lineage being discussed
panels.action: Inside a simple ancestral house, elders gesture toward a scroll while young Recherla Rudra listens, thoughtful, as they speak of their forebear Brahma-sena-pati.

dialogue.text: The Palampet pillar traces Rudra’s line from Brahma-sena-pati, a military chief, not an ancient king. For this family, prestige lay in command, not in royal blood.

i18n.hi: पलमपेट का स्तंभ रुद्र की वंशरेखा ब्रह्मसेनापति से जोड़ता है — एक फौजी सरदार, कोई प्राचीन राजा नहीं। इस कुल की प्रतिष्ठा राजरक्त में नहीं, नेतृत्व में थी

panels.shot: dynamic wide of Rudra’s cavalry riding across dry plains toward distant hills
panels.action: Recherla Rudra leads a column of cavalry across dusty Telangana plains, banners fluttering, distant village mounds and temple towers marking the landscape.

dialogue.text: On campaign, Rudra rode across these plains, where tanks shimmered and stone shrines rose. Land, water and temples were the fabric of Kakatiya power he helped defend.

i18n.hi: युद्ध यात्राओं में रुद्र इन्हीं मैदानों पर घोड़े दौड़ाता था, जहाँ टैंक चमकते थे और पत्थर के देवालय उठते थे। ज़मीन, पानी और मंदिर ही उस काकतीय ताकत की बुनियाद थे जिसे वह बचाता था

panels.shot: tense mid-wide of Rudra confronting armed local rebels near a village
panels.action: Near a village edge, Recherla Rudra faces a group of tense local rebels, his hand firm on his sword hilt, his men behind him, the village fields and houses stretching away.

dialogue.text: Later records at Ramakrishnapuram and Nattaramesvaram recall Rudra suppressing rebels. Holding the kingdom meant not only war at its edges, but order in its villages.

i18n.hi: रामकृष्णपुरम और नटारामेश्वरम के बाद के लेख रुद्र के बगावत दबाने की याद रखते हैं। राज संभालना सिर्फ सीमा पर युद्ध नहीं, गाँवों में अनुशासन भी था

panels.shot: medium shot of Rudra before a damaged temple image of Ganapati
panels.action: In a quiet temple interior, Recherla Rudra stands solemnly before a worn and tilted stone image of Ganapati, lamps flickering and priests watching anxiously.

dialogue.text: The same inscriptions praise him for restoring Ganapati. To a Kakatiya commander, healing sacred images was part of mending the world he was sworn to guard.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं लेखों में उसे गणपति की पुनर्स्थापना के लिए सराहा गया है। एक काकतीय सेनानायक के लिए मूरतों को फिर से स्वस्थ करना उस दुनिया को जोड़ने का हिस्सा था जिसकी रक्षा की उसने शपथ ली थी

panels.shot: architectural wide of Palampet tank and rising temple skeleton, workers busy
panels.action: At Palampet, a vast tank glows as artisans and laborers swarm over the growing Rudreshvara temple, scaffolds and carved blocks everywhere, while Rudra oversees the work from the embankment.

dialogue.text: By 1213, Rudra turned from battlefield to building. At Palampet, he commissioned the Rudreshvara temple beside a great tank, binding devotion, water and stone into one project.

i18n.hi: १२१३ तक रुद्र रणभूमि से निर्माण की ओर मुड़ा। पलमपेट में उसने एक बड़े टैंक के किनारे रुद्रेश्वर मंदिर बनवाया, भक्ति, पानी और पत्थर को एक ही योजना में बाँध दिया

panels.shot: focused medium shot of Rudra speaking with Ramappa, the master architect
panels.action: On a half-built mandapa, Recherla Rudra stands in discussion with the craftsman Ramappa, who holds carving tools and gestures toward ornate pillars and friezes.

dialogue.text: Tradition remembers Ramappa here as master architect and sculptor. The deity was Rudreshvara, but the artistry gave the complex a second, human name that outlived titles.

i18n.hi: परंपरा यहाँ रामप्पा को मुख्य वास्तुकार और मूर्तिकार के रूप में याद रखती है। देवता रुद्रेश्वर थे, पर शिल्पकला ने इस परिसर को एक दूसरा, मानवीय नाम दिया जो पदवियों से भी लंबा चला

panels.shot: wide interior of Rudreshvara garbhagriha being prepared, priests and Rudra present
panels.action: Inside the dim sanctum, priests tend a linga of Rudreshvara as Recherla Rudra watches, palms joined, carved walls closing around them like a stone cocoon.

dialogue.text: The pillar calls the god Rudreshvara. Rudra’s own name echoes in the deity, but the record keeps them distinct. Commander and god stand side by side, not as one.

i18n.hi: स्तंभ में देवता को रुद्रेश्वर कहा गया है। रुद्र का अपना नाम देव में गूंजता है, पर लेख उन्हें अलग रखता है। सेनानायक और देवता साथ खड़े हैं, एक नहीं

panels.shot: medium shot of scribes and stone masons drafting and chiseling the inscription text
panels.action: Scribes sit cross-legged drafting text on palm leaves while stone masons carefully chisel those lines into the pillar shaft, with Rudra watching, measuring the height with his gaze.

dialogue.text: Line after line, scribes and sculptors carved his world: his lineage from Brahma-sena-pati, his offices, his grants, and the temple whose rituals and lands he set in order.

i18n.hi: पंक्ति दर पंक्ति, लेखक और शिल्पकारों ने उसकी दुनिया तराशी: ब्रह्मसेनापति से उसकी वंशरेखा, उसके पद, उसके दान, और वह मंदिर जिसकी भूमि और अनुष्ठान उसने व्यवस्थित किए

panels.shot: medium shot of Rudra instructing village headmen with a map and palm-leaf grants
panels.action: In an open pavilion, Recherla Rudra points to a rough map of local villages as headmen listen; palm-leaf documents bearing grant details lie spread before them.

dialogue.text: The pillar details grants to Nekkonda and other villages. Through such endowments, Rudra tied rural revenues to temple lamps, turning land into ritual and local elites into partners.

i18n.hi: स्तंभ में नेककोंडा और अन्य गाँवों को दिए दान दर्ज हैं। ऐसे दान से रुद्र ने गाँव की आमदनी को मंदिर की बातियों से जोड़ा, ज़मीन को रीत में और स्थानीय मुखियाओं को सहभागी में बदला

panels.shot: low-angle of the pillar being raised upright by ropes and workers as Rudra supervises
panels.action: Workers strain on ropes as the massive inscribed pillar is heaved upright beside the temple tank; Recherla Rudra stands nearby, steady, as the stone slowly finds its vertical stance.

dialogue.text: When the pillar rose, it fixed a moment in Kakatiya time: a commander’s service, a temple’s birth, and a pattern of shared power between court, commanders and countryside.

i18n.hi: जब यह स्तंभ उठा, उसने काकतीय समय का एक क्षण थाम लिया: एक सेनानायक की सेवा, एक मंदिर का जन्म, और दरबार, सेनानायकों व देहात के बीच बाँटी हुई ताकत की एक रीत

panels.shot: reflective close-up on Rudra’s face at dusk, pillar looming behind
panels.action: At dusk, Recherla Rudra looks up at the now-standing pillar, his face lined by campaign and responsibility, the engraved surface catching the last light behind him.

dialogue.speaker: recherla_rudra
dialogue.text: Let it remember not my name alone, but the order we built.

i18n.hi: याद रहे सिर्फ मेरा नाम नहीं, वह व्यवस्था भी जो हमने गढ़ी

panels.shot: documentary-style montage of later inscriptions at Ramakrishnapuram and Nattaramesvaram
panels.action: A visual montage shows stone slabs at Ramakrishnapuram and Nattaramesvaram, their inscriptions highlighted, echoing Rudra’s name and deeds in later, related records.

dialogue.text: By 1218, other inscriptions at Ramakrishnapuram and Nattaramesvaram still spoke of Rudra: of rebels put down, of Ganapati restored, of the same web of officers around Warangal.

i18n.hi: १२१८ तक रामकृष्णपुरम और नटारामेश्वरम के अन्य लेख अभी भी रुद्र की बात करते हैं: दबाई गई बगावतों की, सुधारे गए गणपति की, और वरंगल के चारों ओर वही अधिकारियों के जाल की

panels.shot: modern-era wide shot of present-day Palampet temple complex and pillar, tourists small
panels.action: In the present day, the Rudreshvara temple and Palampet pillar stand weathered but proud, with visitors walking quietly around the tank and carved mandapas.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars read these stones to trace ministerial and commander networks. Rudra’s pillar becomes a map of how middle powers once served, negotiated and anchored the Kakatiya state.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान इन पत्थरों को पढ़कर मंत्रियों और सेनानायकों के नेटवर्क जोड़ते हैं। रुद्र का स्तंभ दिखाता है कि कभी मध्यम शक्तियाँ काकतीय राज्य की सेवा, सौदेबाज़ी और नींव कैसे बनती थीं

panels.shot: final contemplative close-up of a single inscribed line on the pillar fading into sky
panels.action: An extreme close-up on one weathered inscribed line on the pillar slowly widens into the open sky above Palampet, the temple silhouette faint at the horizon.

dialogue.text: Recherla Rudra did not claim a throne; he claimed responsibility. His pillar still asks us whether our own service will fade with us, or stand as structures others can live within.

i18n.hi: रेचेर्ला रुद्र ने सिंहासन नहीं माँगा; उसने ज़िम्मेदारी माँगी। उसका स्तंभ आज भी पूछता है कि हमारी सेवा हमारे साथ मुरझा जाएगी, या ऐसी रचना बनकर खड़ी होगी जिसमें दूसरे जी सकें

title_i18n.hi: पलमपेट में रेचेर्ला रुद्र का स्तंभ

subtitle_i18n.en: A commander carves his service into stone beneath the Kakatiya sky
subtitle_i18n.hi: काकतीय आसमान के नीचे एक सेनानायक अपनी सेवा पत्थर पर उकेरता है
